contract: Road user a overtakes and passes road user b: travelling with headings aligned, a goes from wholly behind b to wholly ahead of it. a is wholly behind b at an observation where drv.position.behind of a relative to b holds and drv.position.behind of b relative to a does not; a is wholly ahead of b where drv.position.behind of b relative to a holds and drv.position.behind of a relative to b does not. Where both hold, as headings that are aligned but not parallel allow for bodies apart sideways, a is neither wholly behind nor wholly ahead of b. The act is recognized at the observation at which a becomes wholly ahead of b, provided that a was wholly behind b at an earlier observation and the headings stayed aligned (rel.same_direction with the alignment tolerance) at every observation from that one to the recognition. Its observed beginning is the last observation at which a was wholly behind b before the recognition. The concept holds at the recognition observation only. Where the recording shows no observation of a wholly behind b before a becomes wholly ahead of it, with the headings aligned at every observation since the recording began, whether a overtook b is unknown, never false. Not a stand-in for a lane change or for contact between the bodies; it does not say in which lane either travels.

params.name: alignment
params.meaning: the cosine of the largest angle between the two headings counted as aligned

act.onset: Its observed beginning is the last observation at which a was wholly behind b before the recognition.
act.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which a becomes wholly ahead of b
act.extent: The concept holds at the recognition observation only.
act.history: Where the recording shows no observation of a wholly behind b before a becomes wholly ahead of it, with the headings aligned at every observation since the recording began, whether a overtook b is unknown, never false.

elements.span: drv.position.behind of a relative to b holds and drv.position.behind of b relative to a does not
elements.justification: drv.position.behind: 'Road user a is behind road user b at an observation: their headings are aligned and b's body lies wholly ahead of a's along a's heading', measured in a's own frame; with headings aligned but not parallel each user can be behind the other in its own frame, so a is wholly behind b only where a is behind b and b is not behind a. This makes wholly behind and wholly ahead exclusive, so the observation of a wholly behind b is necessarily earlier than the recognition.

elements.span: drv.position.behind of b relative to a holds and drv.position.behind of a relative to b does not
elements.justification: drv.position.behind read the other way: b behind a ('b's body lies wholly ahead of a's along a's heading' with the roles exchanged) and not a behind b; its becoming true is the recognition.

elements.span: the headings stayed aligned (rel.same_direction with the alignment tolerance)
elements.justification: rel.same_direction: 'headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance'; held at every observation from the beginning to the recognition, so an oncoming crossing is no pass.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: a, in the left lane wholly behind b with aligned headings, comes alongside and becomes wholly ahead of b; the concept holds at that observation.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: a comes alongside b and stays alongside to the end of the recording, never wholly ahead.

differs_from.why: drv.position.behind states a relative position at one observation; this concept states an act over time: a passing from wholly behind b to wholly ahead of it, recognized at the observation of the change, with the headings aligned from the beginning to the recognition and an unknown verdict where the beginning lies before the recording. It calls drv.position.behind both ways rather than rebuilding it.
